# Generated native application service fixture

This application owns a real channel-driven native thread and its joined close future. The CLI test writes the actual generated registrant to `LEPTOSKIT_SERVICE_FIXTURE_OUTPUT`; build this fixture with `SERVICE_REGISTRANT_DIR` naming that directory. Use the same explicit Cargo/rustc toolchain as the parent test and a separate target directory. The compiler includes the generated registrant directly.

The CLI hybrid generation test also writes its actual Rust, Android, iOS, and macOS registrants to `LEPTOSKIT_HYBRID_FIXTURE_OUTPUT` when set. Point `SERVICE_REGISTRANT_DIR` there to exercise the hybrid constructor. The maintained `generated/` callers are compared with actual generated native source. `android/Platform.kt` and `apple/PlatformPlugin.swift` implement the same echo capability for compilation with the real platform bridge; each accepts the generated host's context and uses the distinct `fixture-platform` identity. Native source generation and the Rust ABI fixture are separate checks; run the Swift/Kotlin callers on their actual hosts before claiming platform execution.

The executable checks constructor failure before task creation, inert registration, activation, real task completion and wake, Pending close, and native join before close succeeds. It registers `fixture-platform` through the native dispatcher's real C ABI before activating the Rust service, which registers `fixture-session`. It asserts that both identities survive and that a duplicate native registration fails without replacing either capability. It runs on the native host; it does not establish Swift/Kotlin dispatcher or installed desktop, Android or iOS execution. Its service intentionally has no Solana dependency. A Solana integration belongs to application-owned client code; on-chain programs use Pina or official Solana program libraries.
